phthalate_dehp_eq.basis: Group TDI, reduction in fetal testosterone; DEHP-eq = 1 DEHP + 5 DBP + 4 DIBP + 0.1 BBP (Reg. 2023/1442 group 36). Temporary TDI.

antimony.basis: NOAEL 6.0 mg/kg bw/day (90-day rat study) / UF 1000.

antioxidant_i168.basis: NOEL 2000 ppm in a 2-year rat study, safety factor 100; covers Irgafos 168 and its phosphate.

lead.basis: No safe intake exists for lead, so EFSA withdrew the tolerable weekly intake and uses a benchmark dose (developmental neurotoxicity in children, BMDL01). The % shown is of this reference point, not of a safe limit.

paperboard_tray.reason_en: The old worry was PFAS coatings, which US food packaging dropped in 2024.

paper_cup.reason_en: It's lined with a thin plastic film. Lab tests found traces of lead in hot water from these cups.

takeout_tub.reason_en: Not made for heat. It can warp or melt.

pet_clamshell.reason_en: It softens around 150°F, cooler than reheated food.

eps_foam.reason_en: Not made for heat. It can warp or melt.

ps_rigid.reason_en: It's only made for up to 170°F. Reheated food gets hotter.

metal.reason_en: Metal can spark in the microwave.

melamine.reason_en: Not for hot food or the microwave. Heat can make it release chemicals.

ceramic.reason_en: No plastic touches your food. Skip plates with gold or silver trim.

stove_pot.reason_en: The food comes out of the package, so no plastic gets heated.

popcorn_bag.reason_en: US popcorn bags no longer use PFAS coatings.

susceptor_sleeve.reason_en: These get much hotter than boiling, so I can't estimate them.

paper_cup.conditions: 20 PE-lined paper cups, 200 mL ultrapure water at 95-100 C, 15 min. Value per litre of water applied per kg of soup or noodles.
